# OMP Session Gateway

> Native integration with stock Oh My Pi (OMP) >=18.1.20. No OMP fork, custom build,
> gateway-specific OMP plugin, or publisher credential. Stable v0.7.2 is published as immutable
> GitHub Latest. Keep using OMP in the terminal; the separate gateway discovers collaboration-enabled
> sessions and opens OMP's own encrypted View/Control client in any modern browser, installable as a PWA where the platform supports it. One-time
> setup requires collab.autoStart, Bun 1.4.0, gateway installation, and TUN-mode Tailscale Serve
> with Funnel disabled. No per-session QR scan or link copy. Community project; not affiliated
> with or endorsed by the Oh My Pi maintainers.

## Supported platforms

- Supported and tested in CI on every change (the stock-OMP canaries run daily): Linux, macOS, and Windows gateway hosts; Chrome and Chromium, Edge through Chromium, Firefox, Safari/WebKit, and Android; iPhone and iPad as a WebKit browser, emulated in CI. Supported is not qualified: qualification is the exact hardware matrix below. Lanes: portable-source (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows), browser-core (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, iPhone-class WebKit), browser-notifications (Pixel sizes), windows-service-lifecycle, canary and canary-windows.

## Current qualification boundary

- Stable v0.7.2 (source af81ac2b90292bd62212019651f4d597bd2645fc, archive SHA-256 98bb3aba1338ee0f0f53076b5fd95c474cd2d9f71981599c148a898dfa572f6a) was promoted from signed candidate v0.7.2-prealpha.2 with identical runtime bytes, qualified against stock OMP v18.4.8 built from source. There are no gateway runtime fixes since v0.7.1. Stable v0.7.2 was published 2026-10-02 at 12:37:44 UTC as GitHub Latest; published v0.7.1 is the predecessor. All thirteen lanes passed on their first attempt in the 2026-10-02 campaign, 11:32:08Z–12:20:54Z, orchestrator 5e167f4ea11060c1563a5bdd84587fb3d76f311e. Earlier failed and stopped attempts are recorded in the release ledger. No claim for arbitrary builds from main.
- Exact OMP v18.4.8 source: 717f97f4d22b3d65c4a4eef6a744255d46f4d1a6. Set only collab.autoStart (off/view/control); start participating sessions with plain omp. The gateway reads OMP discovery and queries each host; OMP does not register with the gateway. The embedded client retains its v18.4.2 provenance and wire pin.
- Debian lane: run 37001605048 succeeded against the candidate archive with stock OMP v18.4.8 built from source. The export does not enumerate OS/kernel versions or migration/recovery invariant counts.
- Mac17,14 / macOS 27.0.1 arm64, the Mac Studio: stock OMP v18.4.8 built from source, native addon b9a905e063b3, doctor 18/18, rollback 23/23. This is the first campaign on the Studio; earlier Mac receipts remain historical.
- Windows x86-64, build 26100, disposable VM with 4 CPUs and 8,186 MiB reported memory: as Administrator, the candidate upgraded published v0.7.1, passed a real reboot with three pre-login samples over 61,655 ms, and started automatically 66,309 ms after interactive logon; doctor 15/18 with only the tagged node's identity, PWA and session checks false; named-pipe generation 1, View/Control 200, stale generations 409, all no-store; Pixel View/Control, readiness rotation, history-selected rollback, restoration and uninstall passed. A fresh standard-account install without Administrator membership or SeSecurityPrivilege passed three pre-login samples over 46,826 ms, automatic start 34,368 ms after logon, doctor 15/18, rotation and uninstall. Configuration and readiness were preserved. The VM, firewall, tailnet node and access vault were removed. The claim is interactive logon, not boot; standard-account upgrade and rollback are not qualified.
- Stock OMP v18.4.8 publication: generation-1 View/Control returned 200 with capability and no-store; host revoked. New-generation and fork transitions kept the instance, advanced generation by 1, rejected stale launches and each allowed two live launches; fork used two synthetic messages. Resume created a new instance at generation 1 with the same label, two live launches and two revocations.
- Pixel 10 Pro / Android 17 build CP3A.260905.009 / Chrome 154.0.8037.57: View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted, return to directory; same-page recovery: unlock 6,584 ms, Airplane 3,671 ms, Doze 301 ms; all seven forbidden capability sinks detectable and clean.
- Background Web Push on the Pixel, installed WebAPK: Private, Session and Preview lock-screen delivery in 1,349, 1,555 and 1,561 ms respectively, one notification each; current Control and View taps, stale-generation scrub without a launch, authoritative clear, triage with zero mutations, stale taps scrubbed without a launch, permission revocation, lock/resume, Wi-Fi and cellular delivery, Airplane suppression and recovery; ten forbidden sinks detectable and clean. Force-stop delivered_while_force_stopped and Doze delivered_after_doze_exit are observed variants, never delivery guarantees. Device, browser and fixture restored.
- TestingBot real cloud browsers through tunnel 4.9: iPhone 17 Pro Max / iOS 26.6 / Safari 26.6, iPad (9th generation) / iPadOS 26.6 / Safari 26.6, Galaxy S25 (SM-S931B) / Android 15.0.0 / Chrome 149.0.7827.159. Each matched the candidate app asset and passed View read-only, Control writable, prompt accepted, return to directory and seven detectable clean sinks. Tunnel refusals: 11, 24 and 26 respectively; three vendor records exposed no links or media. The iPhone Home Screen app enabled alerts with an expirationTime-omitting subscription on web.push.apple.com; delivery took 4,430 ms, the tap opened current Control with a scrubbed address, and alerts were then disabled. Cloud cleanup restored. The export does not identify the tunnel host or observed Serve identity. This is not a lock-screen claim; lock, Airplane, Doze, force-stop and cellular behavior stay Pixel-only.
- Tailscale Serve over tailnet HTTPS only, TUN mode required, Funnel disabled. Fresh relay check: 1,800 seconds (2026-10-02T11:45:46.097Z–12:15:46.107Z), two transitions, final phase live. This replaces the eight-hour gate; eight-hour endurance and bounded memory growth are not claimed. Final cleanup measured zero gateway processes, zero listeners and zero live OMP hosts.
- Attention and lifecycle qualification is limited to the recorded retained-Mac new-generation/fork/resume and Pixel triage/stale-tap scenarios, not arbitrary behavior on every platform. Other Windows builds, desktop Safari and new media qualification remain outside this exact claim. Android radio changes can still wedge Chrome; the proven same-page recoveries do not remove that limit.
- v0.7.1 is the migration/rollback predecessor. Both versions embed the same OMP 18.4.2 collaboration client and wire pin; there are no gateway runtime fixes to undo. Gateway rollback does not switch OMP. Retained-runtime selection and earlier predecessor limits are recorded in the upgrade/rollback document.
- In v0.5.0 and earlier, the first visit after a gateway upgrade can navigate a pending launch or an open View/Control page back to the directory: the service worker cannot see that a page is in use because Chromium reports each page's creation URL. The first post-release View/Control smoke failures match this navigation. The v0.5.1 fix never navigates from the worker.
- The v0.7.2 published-byte local/Pixel smoke passed on its second attempt against Bun's global stock OMP 18.1.20, not reinstalled. The first attempt had already upgraded the gateway to 0.7.2-0e6104d6ee0b but failed at the installed-WebAPK check's two-second sample; #346 corrected the tooling to wait up to 30 s for the launched task, still failing closed. The passing run reported installed: false, configPreserved: true, readinessTokenPreserved: true, and doctorChecks: 18; Tailscale Serve was unchanged with unrelated mappings preserved. Pixel View was read-only and Control writable; capability-sink, same-page recovery and installed-WebAPK checks passed. Gateway, mainline OMP and WebAPK were left installed. The retained development candidate 0.7.2-737c81e5d92f is the plain rollback target; published predecessor 0.7.1-2c4f80b3ccc2 is retained one step further back. This smoke runs on macOS and does not expand the candidate matrix: Windows rests on its lane, iPhone, iPad and Galaxy browsers on the cloud lane, background Push on the Pixel lane, and exact stock OMP v18.4.8 on the candidate evidence.

## Fork-era release history

- v0.3.0 requires its exact patched OMP v18.1.14 and matching historical instructions. Its qualification does not transfer to the mainline architecture.
